summary: John Brockington is an Indologist who served as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Edinburgh, attested in 1987 and 2003.

John Brough was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics scholar. He studied at Edinburgh under Arthur Berriedale Keith and Cambridge under Harold Walter Bailey, later holding professorships at the University of London (1950) and the University of Cambridge (1967-1984).
John Buescher is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed his doctoral dissertation at the University of Virginia in 1982 and served as Director at Voice of America (attested 2001).
John C. Huntington was a scholar in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He served as a professor at Ohio State University, attested from 1987 to 1990 and in 2000.

John C. Maraldo worked in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He held posts at the University of North Florida, attested in 1988 and later as distinguished professor emeritus of philosophy in 2015.
John Chadwick was a linguist and archaeologist. He was educated at St Paul's School and Corpus Christi College, Cambridge, and held a post at the University of Cambridge from circa 1952 to 1984.
John Claude White was a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied at Rugby School and the Royal Indian Engineering College between circa 1873 and 1876.

John Clifford Holt is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Gustavus Adolphus College, GTU, and the University of Chicago under Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah, and was a Professor of Religion at Bowdoin College (~1978-2020).
John Collinson Nesfield was an Indology and linguistics scholar who completed his studies at Highgate School and Merton College (~1855-1860).

John Corrigan is a scholar of religious studies and history who studied at the University of Chicago (~1978-1982). His career includes academic appointments at Harvard, the University of Virginia, Arizona State University, and Florida State University.

John Crook, a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studied at Southampton, Jesus College, and under Sheng Yen, founding the Western Chan Fellowship in 1997. He held posts at the University of Bristol and Université Bouddhique Européenne.

John D. Dunne is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at CIHTS and Harvard, and has held academic posts at Harvard, Antioch College, the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1999), and Emory University (~2005-2016).
John Daido Loori was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under and succeeded Taizan Maezumi. He served as the Abbot of Zen Mountain Monastery from circa 1980 to 2009.
John Daishin Buksbazen is a figure in Buddhist studies who studied at the Zen Center of Los Angeles under teachers Taizan Maezumi and Bernie Glassman (attested 2002).
John Dowson was an Indologist and linguist who held positions at University College London and served as Professor of Hindustani at the Staff College, Camberley (~1855-1877).
John E. Cort is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and Harvard University. He became a professor at Denison University circa 1993.

John Faithfull Fleet was an Indologist and epigraphist who studied at University College London (~1865-1867). He served in the Bombay and Indian Civil Services (~1867-1897) and was Epigraphist for the Government of India (1883-1886).

John Gombojab Hangin was an Iranian/Central Asian studies scholar and linguist. Educated at Hokkaido, Columbia, and Indiana universities, he held academic positions at Johns Hopkins, Georgetown, UC Berkeley, Columbia, and Indiana University (1964-1989).
John H. Berthrong was a scholar of sinology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under Alfonso Verdu and held a post at Boston University from circa 1989 to 2017.

John Henry Wright was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. After studying at Dartmouth College (~1869-1873), he held posts at Johns Hopkins University (~1886-1887) and served as Professor at Harvard University (~1887-1908).
